entries.proposition: The Results state 1783 patients (1521 children and 217 adult females) aged 5 days to 69 years.
entries.snippet: A total of 1783 patients—1521 children and 217 adult females—ranging in age from 5 days to 69 years were included.

entries.proposition: The adverse-event table gives N = 1738 as the all-patients denominator.
Median age of the paediatric group at baseline is 2.0 years (IQR 0.8 to 5.6) and the median sirolimus dose is 0.6 mg (IQR 0.4 to 0.8).
The paediatric median dose in Table 1 is 0.6 mg (IQR 0.4 to 0.8).
Dosing was 1 mg per square metre per day to a maximum of 2 mg, titrated over 2 weeks to a trough of 5 to 10 ng/ml.
entries.snippet: starting dosage of 1 mg/m2/day, with a maximum dose of 2 mg. Dose adjustments were made by a 2-week titration period to attain a trough blood concentration of 5 to 10 ng/ml

entries.proposition: Median follow-up was 25 months (IQR 12 to 43); 380 patients were followed over 4 years, 21 over 8 years and 4 reached 10 years.
entries.snippet: The median follow-up duration was 25 months (IQR: 12–43 months), with 380 individuals followed for over 4 years, 21 for over 8 years, and 4 reaching a 10-year follow-up.

entries.proposition: Among the paediatric group, dose was the only factor associated with all three growth Z-score categories, with ORs above 2 or below 0.5.
entries.snippet: showed that the dose of sirolimus was the only factor significantly associated with all three variables with ORs more than 2 or less than 0.5 (Table 2)

entries.proposition: The authors describe the conclusion on growth as 'Sirolimus does not negatively affect the physical growth of pediatric patients' while stating there is no control group.
entries.snippet: Although there is no control group, this study has set up the safety profile of sirolimus in actual clinical scenarios

entries.proposition: Stomatitis was reported in 920 of 1738 patients (52.9 percent) and usually resolved within a week.
entries.snippet: stomatitis as the most frequent condition (920/1738 cases, 52.9%), and it usually resolved within a week

entries.proposition: Menstrual irregularities are printed as 48.5 percent of adult females (112 of 217), lasting 6 to 24 months, the longest 80 months.
entries.snippet: Menstrual irregularities affected 48.5% of adult females (112 of 217), with durations ranging from 6 to 24 months, and the longest case lasting 80 months.

entries.proposition: One patient died of an unknown cause after two years of therapy; the cause was not reported.
entries.snippet: Another patient, however, died from an unknown cause after two years of therapy.

entries.proposition: 38 participants discontinued, with adverse effects prompting cessation in seven (one recurrent stomatitis, six recurrent infections).
entries.snippet: Medication discontinuation was observed in 38 participants at different stages of follow-up, with adverse effects directly prompting cessation in seven instances: one due to recurrent stomatitis and six due to recurrent infections.

entries.proposition: The text reports transient rises in RBC, WBC, HGB and PLT within the first year, returning to baseline, citing Fig. 2.
entries.snippet: Transient increases in RBC, WBC, HGB, and PLT levels were noted within the first year of follow-up, subsequently returning to baseline values (Fig. 2).

entries.proposition: The authors raise a possible dose-response reversal above a threshold and call the result preliminary.
entries.snippet: Our findings suggest that the effects of sirolimus may exhibit a certain dose-response reversal effect.
